item.title: America needs a Space Academy for the space age
item.description: The United States is moving its space activity outward, from low Earth orbit to the moon, cislunar space and beyond. Rockets and spacecraft are the visible part of that expansion. The harder problem is people. The country needs leaders who can run an enterprise that grows more complicated every year, and a U.S. Space Academy would help supply them.

item.title: The attrition advantage: Why passive mobility is essential for resilient sensor architectures
item.description: The modern battlefield has reached a dangerous tipping point. Our most expensive assets are now often our most vulnerable. For decades, United States defense strategy has relied on exquisite, stationary radar installations that delivered performance. But inexpensive drones and missiles can now threaten radar systems worth hundreds of millions of dollars, creating an increasingly unfavorable cost and survivability equation.
